summary: 1. 2026-10-12 -- scope resolution for the three items flagged 2026-10-11 ("JRAR Reports", the dispatch tyre report, `Production report/Other Reports/`), per Peter's decision in chat Peter's decision on each: ingest both JRAR Reports docx and document the figure conflict rather than resolve it; ingest and compile the tyre report now; register `Production report/Other Reports/` as a recurring RAW location, ingesting the GM Weekly Meeting deck (already done by an earlier pass), the Maaden Performance Review decks, and Production Main Sheets now, with the Dispatch WhatsApp media registered at index level only. `CLAUDE.md`'s RAW Folder Layout section updated with both new locations. 2. Read and compiled: both September JRAR Reports docx (Original and Joe Revised), the Sep 1-Oct 10 dispatch tyre report `.msg` plus its attached by-dispatch PDF, the Q3 2026 and September 2026 Maaden Performance Review decks, and the September Production Main Sheets master workbook (structure only). 3. Registered by name only: the other eight months of Production Main Sheets, the Dispatch WhatsApp/voice-note dump, and the GM Weekly Meeting WhatsApp image. 4. Findings Joe Revised reframes September's ore-mined variance as +1% (160,604t budget / 161,717t achieved) against the already-ingested PDF's +9% (146,986t / 160,604t) — the budget figure in one version is the achieved figure in the other. 5. Not resolved; flagged for Peter to check with Joe directly. 6. Joe Revised adds a nine-event, 43,000 BCM / 98h September production-loss table with no equivalent in the PDF: largest single event is an 18-Sep dust suppression stand-down (10,800 BCM/18h), followed by a 20-Sep fuel bowser delay (13,600 BCM/6h) and a 10-Sep water truck breakdown (4,000 BCM/45h). 7. Tyre report: Sep 1-Oct 10 totals 670.95h / 27.96 days across 65 incidents, 528.45h / 22.02 days of that on dump trucks — matches the Oct 11 HOD meeting's figures exactly. 8. One entry, DT-346's 822.75-hour "Replace Tire" record (04-Aug to 07-Sep), exceeds the report's own stated total on its own and starts a month before the report's "01 Sep" window — doesn't reconcile, flagged as an open question. 9. The Q3 and September Performance Review decks (dated 12-Oct, the day of Maaden's own contractor review) name August's lead equipment faults with hours for the first time: CAT 6015 (Ex-253) swing fault, 679h/~157,700 BCM est.; CAT 6020 track/hydraulic failures, 324h/~73,500 BCM est. — combined estimate exceeds August's own 127,513 BCM shortfall against plan. The Production Main Sheets master workbook (one `.xlsm` per month) sits upstream of the whole [[production-data-stack]] model — per-unit tabs plus the same Client Meeting Report / A&U / DPR / Daily KPI content already tracked, one level closer to source. Its per-day tabs hold only the latest day's snapshot, not a running history; the Production BCM tab is the exception. Eight of the nine Production Main Sheets months (Jan-Aug 2026) were registered by name only, not opened. The Dispatch WhatsApp/voice-note dump and the GM Weekly Meeting WhatsApp image were registered at index level per Peter's decision, not analyzed.
